title: Close substrate gap recommit-child-gaps-describe-the-failure-instead-of-the-change-wanted. Edit repos/development-vessel
description:
Close substrate gap recommit-child-gaps-describe-the-failure-instead-of-the-change-wanted. Edit repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/feature-compose.ts.

When a compose fails, it mints a recommit- child gap whose summary is built from the PREVIOUS FAILURE'S RAW OUTPUT rather than from the change that was wanted. Measured across 400 open gaps: recommit- children have a median summary of 253 characters with 90 percent under 300, against 448 for operator-filed gaps and 1178 for narrowed children. Some summaries are pure build log, for example '== install == == resolve == DRYRUN_EXIT=0'. A drafter handed a description of what went wrong instead of what to do cannot produce a targeted patch, and the semantic gate then correctly rolls the result back.

The parent gap object is already in scope at that line, so its summary — the specification of the change wanted — can be carried forward, with the failure attached only as trailing context.

Replace this exact text, which occurs exactly once in the file:
summary: "compose for gap " + String(gap.id) + " repeated already-recorded failure class " + cls + ": " + reason.slice(0, 150),

with this exact text:
summary: String((gap as { summary?: unknown }).summary ?? "") + " [RETRY: the previous attempt failed with " + cls + " — " + reason.slice(0, 150) + ". The change wanted is described above; do not treat this failure text as the specification.]",

This is one substitution on one line. Declare no new variable and add no new statement. The replacement does not contain the anchor, so applying it twice is a no-op.
